new_statements.quote: Betonung. Die Betonung erfolgt mit wenigen Ausnahmen, die im Wortregister durch Akzente gekennzeichnet sind, auf der vorletzten Silbe. Hiebei sind auch die echten Diphthonge als zweisilbig anzusehen. Ausnahmen: lífaja Schmetterling, láhua Asche, búea Leguan, ámuni jener. Die enklitischen Possess.-Pronomina und das Pluralsuffix re haben keinen Einfluß auf die Betonung. Man sagt also: háta-re, íma-re, tína-ku.
new_statements.translation: Stress. With few exceptions, which are marked by accents in the word list, stress falls on the penultimate syllable. Here the true diphthongs are also to be counted as disyllabic. Exceptions: lífaja 'butterfly', láhua 'ash', búea 'monitor lizard', ámuni 'that one'. The enclitic possessive pronouns and the plural suffix re have no influence on the stress. Thus one says: háta-re, íma-re, tína-ku.

new_statements.rule_in_words: In Wahinama/Manusela (the dialect cluster of which Huaulu is described as a member) stress is regularly on the penultimate syllable of the word/stem; a handful of lexical exceptions carry antepenultimate stress; enclitic possessive suffixes and plural -re are outside the stress domain, so stress stays on the stem penult (háta-re).
new_statements.exceptions: lífaja 'butterfly', láhua 'ash', búea 'monitor lizard', ámuni 'that' (antepenultimate); true diphthongs a͜i, a͜u count as two syllables for stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is for Tauern's 'Wahinama' (= Manusela / Sou Upaa [wha], manu1258; data mainly from Manusela village), which Tauern says is spoken 'from the Wai Samal to the Sapolewa, from the high mountains to the north coast'. Huaulu [hud] is treated as a Manusela dialect by Loski & Loski 1989 and Collins 1983 but has its own ISO/Glottolog code; no statement specific to Huaulu was found. Word-level stress; enclitics (possessives, plural -re) do not shift it.
new_statements.identity_note: No description of Huaulu [hud] huau1237 itself was found (Glottolog 5.1: 0 descriptive refs; only Taber 1996 atlas, Loski & Loski 1989 and Taguchi 1989 surveys). The quoted stress statement is Tauern 1931 on 'Wahinama' = Manusela / Sou Upaa [wha], Glottolog manu1258 (data mainly from Manusela village), the other member of Glottolog's 'Manusela-Huaulu' node manu1263. Loski & Loski 1989:119-120 and Collins 1983:44 treat Huaulu as a Manusela dialect (Alakamat/Huaulu village; 64-72% lexical similarity with the other Manusela varieties per Loski & Loski's Table, reproduced in Grimes & Edwards 2026 Table 10.11), but ISO/Glottolog code it separately; using Tauern's rule for huau1237 would be a sister-lect proxy, hence candidate_for_catalog=false.

sources.note: For Wahinama (= Manusela [wha], material collected mainly in Manusela village): stress on the penultimate syllable with few accent-marked exceptions (lífaja, láhua, búea, ámuni); true diphthongs count as two syllables; enclitic possessive pronouns and plural suffix -re do not affect stress (háta-re, íma-re, tína-ku).
